newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda reports second Heath Steele mishap.
newsitem.headline: Noranda reports second Heath Steele mishap.

text.p: Noranda Inc said on Friday that four miners at its Heath Steele lead and zinc mine in New Brunswick were injured this morning.
The four were in hospital in stable condition after they came in contact with carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide, said Roger Clinch, director of corporate communications for Noranda in New Brunswick.
Underground operations were suspended for the rest of the day, the company said.
The accident is the second this month. On November 4, one miner was killed and another injured after a mine explosion.
Noranda will investigate safety standards at the mine, Clinch said.

"As a result of the events of the past few weeks at Heath Steele, I will initiate an independent investigation of the underground operations at Heath Steele," Derek Pannell, president of Noranda in New Brunswick, said in a statement.

He said he will ask the provincial ministry of mines, the union, the company and an independent investigator to participate. "We remain committed to practicing the highest safety standards possible at our mining operations and I believe that this investigation will enhance our ability to do so."
